subject: Third-party dataflows & contract clauses for regulated deals
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Third-party dataflows & contract clauses for regulated deals

Team,

Merchant Finance is asking for a consolidated view of our contract path for regulated verticals (GLBA + potential BAA ask) and a clean evidence packet they can hand to internal legal/IT. I pulled together a DPA draft and our current subprocessor matrix — attaching below. High level asks from MF legal: residency constraints, list of subprocessors that touch PII/financial data, and confirmation of transfer mechanisms.

Attachment stubs: redwood_dpa_draft_v1.pdf; subprocessor_matrix.csv; kms_export_controls_summary.pdf

Questions I have:
- Do we have an up-to-date assertion on which subprocessors persist tokenized request logs for >30 days? (MF wants 90 days retained in their environment; we prefer shorter).
- For GLBA customers that demand US-only residency, do we have an operational path (Dedicated pool + VPC) that we can commit to contractually?
- What evidence should we hand over now vs. after LOI (SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, data flow diagrams)?

Karthik — can you confirm whether the current Dedicated offering can be scoped to US regions only and whether we can exclude specific public-cloud subprocessor endpoints? Vanessa — can you prepare a short memo on the redline items we expect from a GLBA addendum so I can set expectations with their counsel.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Third-party dataflows & contract clauses for regulated deals

Jordan — quick notes inline.

On Thu, Apr 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Merchant Finance is asking for a consolidated view of our contract path for regulated verticals (GLBA + potential BAA ask) and a clean evidence packet they can hand to internal legal/IT. I pulled together a DPA draft and our current subprocessor matrix — attaching below. High level asks from MF legal: residency constraints, list of subprocessors that touch PII/financial data, and confirmation of transfer mechanisms.

- Residency: yes — Dedicated + Private (VPC) enables us to keep data in a specified region/tenant. For GLBA US-only we can offer an on-prem or Dedicated pool in a US region and lock the routing policy. Need to validate network egress rules with infra for contract language (I can get a firm statement).
- Subprocessors: our matrix is current to within 30 days. For financial data, primary touchpoints are: monitoring/observability pipeline (CloudMetrics), storage (S3-like object store managed by infra partner), and optional managed embeddings cache. If MF requires exclusion of a given subprocessor, that is doable for Dedicated/Private but not for Hosted.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II + last 12 months pen test summary + DFD (data flow diagram) are standard. For GLBA they often want a signed statement on encryption-in-transit and at-rest (we have that). BAA/PHI requests are heavier — we'd need to scope PHI flows and decide whether we accept a BAA (possible but requires PO approval and E&O insurance check).

I can pull a one-page operational statement on residency/egress by EOD tomorrow.

-Karthik

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Elena Torres <merchantfinance-legal@merchantfinance.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 14:25:00 -0000
Subject: Redwood: DPA + subprocessors + residency evidence for Merchant Finance

Hi Elena — nice to connect over email.

Per our call, attaching a DPA draft and our subprocessor matrix so your team can review. Quick clarifications to help your review:

- We can provide a Dedicated (reserved) deployment scoped to US-only regions and can exclude hosted-mode public subprocessors when the customer selects Dedicated or Private deployment.
- For hosted customers we cannot contractually exclude specific cloud infra subprocessors (standard cloud provider terms).
- Standard evidence we can share pre-LOI: SOC 2 Type II report, data flow diagram for the relevant integration pattern, pen-test executive summary, and the list of subprocessors with roles (we will flag which subprocessors store logs >30 days).
- If you anticipate a BAA ask (PHI), please flag immediately — that requires a different legal addendum and internal approvals (we will need to review the exact PHI flows and acceptance of contractual risk).

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v1.pdf; subprocessor_matrix.csv; kms_export_controls_summary.pdf

Next steps we propose:
1) MF legal reviews the DPA draft and marks redlines.
2) We provide the SOC 2 and pen-test summary via the secure drive link.
3) If GLBA-specific language is required (explicit GLBA addendum), Vanessa will propose the redline positions.

Please let me know your preferred timeline for review and whether Merchant Finance requires an NDA/LOI before we provide SOC 2 artifacts.

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive — Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <merchantfinance-legal@merchantfinance.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Anthony Meyer <anthony.meyer@merchantfinance.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Redwood: DPA + subprocessors + residency evidence for Merchant Finance

Jordan — thanks, received. Quick responses from legal:

- We will need a GLBA-specific addendum. Please outline the clauses you are willing to accept vs. those you will mark as "negotiable" (e.g., liability cap carveouts, breach notification timelines).
- SOC 2 Type II and pen-test exec summary are fine to receive via your secure drive; an NDA is not strictly required but we prefer a DocuSign access control to the artifact (we will send a link).
- Residency: Merchant Finance requires a contractual commitment that no subprocessors outside the US will be used to process or store customer financial data for this account. We understand Dedicated is an available path; request a one-paragraph operational statement and a routing/fallback policy that can be attached to the DPA.
- Subprocessors: please highlight which subprocessors are excluded for Dedicated and which ones remain mandatory (e.g., cloud-provider network fabric). Also call out any subprocessors that retain logs >30 days and what data is contained in those logs.

We will have our procurement team open a DocuSign envelope for the DPA and related exhibit once we get the operational statement and the marked redlines.

On the BAA front: at present MF does not expect PHI in scope, but if a later product use will ingest PHI we will re-open that discussion (and expect Redwood to confirm BAA willingness before pilot).

Thanks — Elena
Elena Torres
Senior Counsel, Merchant Finance, Inc.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0000
Subject: Merchant Finance next steps (GLBA addendum + artifacts)

Vanessa / Karthik — Elena replied with their ask (see forwarded text below). Action items: 

- Vanessa: please draft a 1-paragraph operational statement for US-only Dedicated deployments that includes routing/fallback behavior and a short list of mandatory vs. optional subprocessors. Keep language customer-facing (one paragraph plus bullet list). Target: EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik: confirm with infra whether we can provide a contractual guarantee that no subprocessors outside the US will be used for a Dedicated deployment, and whether any mandatory subprocessors (network fabric, provider storage) are US-resident. Also confirm if we can state "no logs persisted >30 days for customer-request-content" or whether some observability logs exceed that. Target: EOD tomorrow.
- I'll prepare the Docusign envelope (we have the draft) and queue SOC 2 + pen-test summary for controlled access.

Thanks — want to move this to procurement fast; MF indicated procurement will issue the DocuSign envelope once we send the operational statement + marked redlines.

Jordan
